description: Redesign the entire UI to a premium dark analytics-dashboard aesthetic that echoes the reference: deep charcoal (not pure black) background, rounded card panels in a lighter dark tone with subtle borders, a narrow left vertical circular-icon sidebar, a top bar with current date + live market indicator + centered search + notifications/avatar, lime-to-emerald green (#a3e635 / #4ade80) accents used sparingly, and a beige/tan (#d4c5a9) premium featured card. Replace the current indigo/purple 'glass' + animated mesh look. Map the aesthetic onto QuantFeed content across all pages. This depends on FEAT-002 landing first (so cards display real live data), though it can begin against the existing data shape.
steps: Update the palette in tailwind.config.js: add charcoal darks (e.g. bg base #0a0a0a, panel #1a1a1a / #1c1c1e, border #2a2a2a), a green accent scale (lime #a3e635, emerald #4ade80), and a beige/tan accent (#d4c5a9). Keep category accent colors but consider softening. Do not remove tokens still referenced until their usages are migrated.

Overhaul app/globals.css: change --background to charcoal (#0a0a0a-#141414 range) with subtle warmth (not pure black). Replace the indigo-glow 'glass-premium' definition (or add a new 'card-premium' class) with the reference card style: background ~#1a1a1a/#1c1c1e, border 1px #2a2a2a, border-radius 16-20px, subtle shadow. Update gradient-text/text-glow to green-based accents. Remove or tone down the animated indigo gradient-mesh and heavy noise overlay so the look is clean charcoal (keep a very subtle vignette if desired). Add a muted secondary text color (#8a8a8a). Keep scrollbar styling but recolor to neutral/green.

Redesign components/Sidebar.tsx to a NARROW vertical icon rail (approx 64-72px wide): a circular logo/mark at top, circular icon buttons for the nav items (Dashboard/home, Network, News, Analysis, Predictions) using lucide icons, active state shown with a green-accent filled/ringed circle, and a profile/logout circular button pinned at the bottom. Use tooltips or aria-labels for the icon-only links. Preserve the existing nav hrefs and next/link + usePathname active detection. Keep it responsive (may collapse/hide on very small screens as today).

Add a shared top bar. Create a new component components/TopBar.tsx rendered in app/layout.tsx (or per-page) containing: LEFT = current date formatted like 'Wednesday, 25 Sep' plus a live MARKET INDICATOR chip (e.g. 'NIFTY' / 'SENSEX' or 'Markets' status with a green up / red down tone). Since there is no guaranteed markets API key, drive the indicator from available data (e.g. overall sentiment from /api/analysis, or a lightweight derived value) and label it honestly; do NOT fabricate a fake precise index number as if it were a real live quote unless a real value is fetched. CENTER = a search input placeholder 'Search here...'. RIGHT = a notification bell icon and a user avatar + name. Style with the new card/charcoal palette and green accents.

Redesign app/page.tsx (Dashboard) into the reference card grid using the new card style: keep DataSourceBadge; include stat cards (Articles Analyzed, News Clusters / Topics, Active Pathways, Market Sentiment) as big-number cards; a 'Trending Threads' list or radial card (from topClusters / topic correlations); the Daily Economic Summary card; a timeline/list of latest headlines WITH timestamps (from articles sorted by publishedAt) with check/dot indicators; and an impact-over-time bar or line chart card (derive from article economicImpactScore or counts per day). Include one beige/tan (#d4c5a9) featured/premium-styled card (e.g. a highlighted insight or CTA). Wire to existing hooks useNews/useAnalysis. Keep loading skeletons.

Restyle app/news/page.tsx, app/analysis/page.tsx, app/predictions/page.tsx to the same card system and palette: replace glass/indigo classes with the new card-premium/charcoal classes and green accents; keep all existing functionality (filters, search, sort, simulator, prediction metrics). Restyle components/NewsCard.tsx, DailySummary.tsx, LoadingSkeleton.tsx (shimmer to neutral/green), PathwaySimulator.tsx, TopicCorrelationsPanel.tsx accordingly.

Restyle app/network/page.tsx and the panels/controls of components/NetworkGraph.tsx to match: dark cards, green accents, refined Inter typography. Do NOT change the 3D graph physics/interaction logic; only restyle surrounding panels, buttons, legends, and the detail/tooltip panels. Node category colors in the 3D scene may stay for legibility.

Do a repo-wide pass for leftover 'indigo'/'purple'/'glass-premium'/'gradient-mesh'/'text-glow' indigo usages and migrate them to the new palette/classes so the look is consistent. Ensure the Inter font (already wired in layout.tsx) is used throughout with tight spacing, large bold stat numbers, and muted gray secondary text.
acceptance_criteria: The app background is deep charcoal (not pure black, not the old indigo mesh) and cards use rounded (~16-20px) lighter-charcoal panels with subtle 1px borders.
The sidebar is a narrow vertical rail of circular icon buttons with a green-accent active state and a bottom profile/logout button; all existing nav routes still work.
A top bar shows the current date, a market/status indicator, a centered 'Search here...' input, and a notification bell + avatar.
Green (#a3e635/#4ade80) accents and at least one beige/tan (#d4c5a9) featured card are present, used sparingly and consistently.
The dashboard shows stat cards, a trending/clusters card, the daily summary, a timestamped headlines timeline, and an impact chart, all populated from the live data hooks.
All five pages (dashboard, network, news, analysis, predictions) share the consistent new card system with no leftover indigo 'glass-premium' styling visible.
'npm run build' and 'npm run lint' both pass after the redesign.
verification: grep -rn 'glass-premium\|gradient-mesh' app components | wc -l  -> expect 0 or only intentionally-migrated references
npm run dev (background) then load / , /news, /analysis, /predictions, /network via curl to confirm 200 responses and no runtime errors in server logs
